### Historical JWT propagation responsibilities

The historical development principle requires the frontend to attach JWTs through `Single-UI-Authorization` for every API call.
It assigns public-key PEM certificate sharing to the microfrontend team.
Application teams use that certificate for JWT validation and follow the linked SDK guidance.

These are source-stated interface responsibilities. Current implementation and accepted certificate distribution require separate evidence.
[Selected source lines 2–6](<../../../evidence/sources/confluence/FM TPT UI Guild/Microfrontend/FMO Post Trade Portal Home/Development Principle - Development Guideline - Onboarding Process/Development Principle/page.md#L2-L6>)

### Tenant dependency operational responsibilities

The internal-packaging option includes dependency management, vulnerability scanning, licensing review, version control, and release governance.
The backend-encapsulation option assigns security, error handling, resilience, audit, and compliance to the tenant backend.
Portal supplies no direct hosting, calling, or management of external runtime dependencies on behalf of tenants.

Tenant teams retain implementation effort, dependency approval, production support, fallback, rollback, and user-impact responsibilities.
These statements retain the supplementary source rule. Effective applicability and exception approval remain unconfirmed.
[Selected source lines 1–54](<../../../evidence/sources/confluence/FM TPT UI Guild/Microfrontend/FMO Post Trade Portal Home/Supplementary Principle_ External Frontend Dependency Control/page.md#L1-L54>)

### Illustrative source application inventory

The introduction names Trade Blotter, Cashflow Blotter, Exception Blotter, Rules Engine, FlowZero for Ratan, Confirmation and Download Report as examples.
These names form an illustrative source inventory. They establish no complete or current application catalog.
[Selected source lines 5–7](<../../../evidence/sources/confluence/FM TPT UI Guild/Microfrontend/FMO Post Trade Portal Home/Portal Design/page.md#L5-L7>)

### Notification store draft contract

The store draft declares string id, user_id, topic, isRead, message, payload, container, module and tile.
It declares muted and isShown as booleans. The existing isRead assignment conflict remains unresolved.
The source proposes Open In New Tile for new or updated records.

Alternatives use React.useEffect on notification.payload or registered application callbacks.
These are draft alternatives and source-specific field declarations. They establish no accepted schema, callback ordering or delivered behavior.

### Specific 2026 and 2027 proposal scope

The proposal expects FSS offboarding and CDUPS/SSDR onboarding in 2026, with PTS, FM SWIFTGATEWAY, MARS and other applications from 2027.
It refines chatbot and NLP workflows across tiles, activity telemetry, a user-based realtime notification bus, persona remaining-work dashboards and OpenFin.
It also proposes datacenter migration. These remain prospective source declarations with unconfirmed current scope.

The SKE auth-service row groups applications with 16 CPU, 32 GB memory, 100 GB storage and four VMs.
The tile-management, telemetry and AI service rows omit their individual sizing cells. The Webserver/UI row also omits sizing.
The Nginx row gives 4 CPU, 8BG memory, no storage value and four VMs. The database row gives 8 CPU, 64 GB memory, 500 GB storage and four VMs.

The source spells the Nginx memory unit 8BG. It does not establish whether application sizing is shared or per service.
These proposed values establish no approved capacity, bill of materials or deployment topology.

The getting-started description gives each platform view a JavaScript context separate from its window.
A view has no DOM representation within that window.
The described design permits moving a view between windows without refreshing or destroying its context.

The example table uses context broadcast with a URL to open a new Portal window.
It uses `raiseIntent` with `fmchannel.fmoportal` and container, module, and tile identifiers for existing platform views.
That path describes opening a workspace tab in all existing platform views.

The example permits separate context and intent handlers in a real implementation.
These transport-to-behavior associations remain historical example intent, pending an agreed versioned production contract.

### Cache reuse and refresh branches

The described refresh checks the base, application-container, and tile entry files. An unchanged tile entry reuses cached chunks.
A changed entry should reference new subsequent files, which are fetched again. Entry loading still requires waiting for current UI assets.
The expiry table leaves MP3/MP4 media outside its stated cache policy.

Reported timing improvements remain observations and supply no measured current performance guarantee.
[Selected source lines 1–45](<../../../evidence/sources/confluence/FM TPT UI Guild/Microfrontend/FMO Post Trade Portal Home/MFE Performance Monitoring/MFE Cache Strategy/page.md#L1-L45>)

### Draft admin schema access predicates

The category draft uses numeric `category_id` and string `ems2_role`, with the latter controlling that category and child records.
The tile draft uses numeric `tile_id` and `category_id`. Its string `ems2_subject` describes drawer visibility.
The authorization draft uses numeric `authorization_id` and `tile_id`, with string `ems2_entity` for drawer visibility.

Each draft entity includes a Boolean disabled flag and creator/updater strings with date fields.
Tile display and route fields are strings, including `isTemplate` in this draft. The current deployed type remains unconfirmed.
The screen draft requires the Admin Module EMS2 entity and subject to see its admin tiles.

### Historical manual field and permission detail

The manual lists `FMO PORTAL ADMIN` subjects `/importmap`, `/category`, and `/tile`.
Its matrix gives READ-WRITE to RATAN_ADMIN, SSI_ADMIN, FSS_ADMIN, STAMP_ADMIN, LOANIQ_ADMIN, and SSDR_ADMIN for those subjects.
Those historical entries select no current cross-tenant write or verification policy. The manual requires technical understanding of drawer and import-map files.

Verification is enabled for an `un-verified` record. Deactivation is enabled for a `verified` record.
Different maker and checker users receive their team role, and each admin function records changes in its own audit-history table.
Tile creation also includes `Is Template?` and `Email Support`, and the API appends `/` to submitted module and tile paths.

The named active import-map endpoint is `/api/auth/v1/fmo/admin/importmap/active`.

### Historical machine-to-machine protocol detail

The reference uses OAuth2 `client_credentials` with Basic-encoded service-account credentials against FMAA. OUD authentication success returns an access-token JWT.
Its failure example returns HTTP 401 with an Unauthorized/password-validation failure response.
The machine passes the token to its secure service. That service calls FMAA introspection with token and identifier parameters.

The reference describes FMAA validation through JWKS. Successful introspection returns user_id, active, token_type, app_id, and expires_in.
Its failure cases distinguish signature verification, token expiry, and token-owner mismatch. The examples encode active as string values.
These are historical reference contracts. No credentials, token values, source-example lifetime, or HTTP tooling option becomes current policy.

### Historical Entra routing and assertion contracts

The historical BFF design uses `POST /v2/sso/login` for OneMFA/OUD and `POST /v3/sso/login` for Entra.
Blank code selects OUD username/password. Present code with blank iss and client_id selects Entra exchange.
Other historical SSO requests select OneMFA. This fallback is superseded by the current user-stated SSO policy.

Post-authentication processing builds profile and EMS2 entitlements, issues both token families, logs analytics and clears the session cookie.
Declared outputs also include drawer data. External dependencies comprise Entra, EMS2 and LDAP.
The design uses a signed RSA client assertion with certificate thumbprint in x5t and the token-endpoint URL in its audience.

It requires secure private-key/certificate storage and rotation. It lists client IDs, tenant, endpoints, key paths, redirect, scopes and timeouts as configuration.
The exchange sends client_id, client_assertion_type, client_assertion, grant_type, scope, code and redirect_uri. It decodes id_token for profile data.
Expected claims are name, given_name, family_name, email, locale and country. The source assumes Entra accepts its x5t assertion.

These remain documented design assumptions. The production profile guide reports missing locale, which limits any implied uniform profile contract.
[Selected source lines 9–68](<../../../evidence/sources/confluence/FM TPT UI Guild/Microfrontend/FMO Post Trade Portal Home/Entra Migration/Post Trade Portal Entra Migration - Phase 1 - UI SSO/UI SSO Entra Design/page.md#L9-L68>)

### Historical phase 1 migration boundaries and prerequisites

The phase 1 assessment targets UI SSO migration from OneMFA to Entra. It places non-production credential migration from OUD to OpenDJ elsewhere.
It places EMS2-to-EMS3 authorization, FMAA tenant-onboarding authentication and self-managed session changes outside phase 1.
Its historical schedule names March non-production work, April technical release, June default switch, and August full decommission.

Technical release requires completed QA verification. The default switch requires tenant regression and sign-off plus no unresolved production issues.
